title: private-deployment-acme-weekly-sync-2026-04-20
content:
Weekly sync notes - ACME private deployment (VPC / on-prem)
Date: 2026-04-20
Owner / note-taker: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood - PM), Liam O'Connor (SRE/Infra), Priya Shah (Solutions Eng), Diego Martinez (Customer Success), Sarah Patel (Security), Ethan Li (ACME eng lead)

Purpose: quick alignment on milestones, outstanding blockers for ACME private deployment (VPC + on-prem options). Capture owners and due dates.

Agenda:
- Quick customer context + priorities (Ethan)
- Infra & networking status (Liam)
- Security & compliance checklist (Sarah)
- Install/ops: on-prem package testing (Priya)
- Rollout plan + cutover milestones (Maya)
- Blockers & actions

Notes / updates:
1) Customer context (Ethan)
- ACME timeline: target pilot cutover week of 2026-05-11; production by end of June if pilot successful.
- Must support VPC peering option for initial rollout; on-prem package desired for later Q3.
- Priority: predictable latency (<80ms p90 for gen requests) and strict data residency.
- ACME has internal infra team available Tues/Thurs mornings for coordination.

2) Networking & infra (Liam)
- VPC peering setup: initial peering request submitted; ACME's network team provided route prefixes yesterday.
- Pending: CIDR conflict check + BGP config validation.
- Test harness: spun up staging cluster (g4dn equiv) replicating customer config for latency tests.
- Progress: KV cache warmup tests show steady-state throughput OK, but cold-start latency spikes on first batch (seen in logs).

3) Security & compliance (Sarah)
- KMS integration: key exchange doc updated; ACME requires HSM-backed key management (customer-managed keys).
- Audit logging: need to enable longer retention for pilot (90 days) - requires additional storage allocation and pricing approval.
- Pending: ACME's infosec asked for a runbook for incident response during pilot.

4) On-prem / install (Priya)
- On-prem package v0.9 deployed to lab for validation. Installer had two flaky steps: kernel module load (requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN) and systemd unit ordering on older RHEL 7 nodes.
- Workaround documented; plan to push installer fixes in v0.9.1.
- Need ACME to provide two representative hardware profiles (CPU/GPU, OS versions) by next week for final validation.

5) Customer success & rollout plan (Diego)
- Pilot scope: 2 apps, internal users only, 2-week pilot window. Rollout gating criteria defined: latency SLOs met, no critical security findings, install repeatability.
- Onboarding docs: Diego to send updated runbook + checklist to ACME by 2026-04-22.

Blockers / Risks:
- B1: CIDR overlap risk between Redwood staging and ACME networks delaying peering (owner: Liam).
- B2: HSM KMS procurement and account linking may take >2 weeks (owner: Sarah + ACME procurement).
- B3: Installer compatibility issues on RHEL7 could delay on-prem validation (owner: Priya).
- B4: Cold-start latency spikes on first requests may violate pilot latency SLO (owner: Liam + runtime team).

Decisions made:
- Use VPC peering for pilot; on-prem package validation continues in parallel but production on-prem later.
- Enable 90-day audit log retention for pilot (pending pricing sign-off from finance).

Action items (owner - due date - status notes):
- AI-1: Liam O'Connor - complete CIDR conflict check and confirm final peering config with ACME by 2026-04-22. (high)
- AI-2: Sarah Patel - finalize HSM/KMS integration runbook + start account provisioning conversation with ACME procurement by 2026-04-27. (blocking)
- AI-3: Priya Shah - push installer fixes for kernel module ordering and systemd units; release v0.9.1 to lab and notify team by 2026-04-24. (in progress)
- AI-4: Priya Shah & Ethan Li - ACME to provide two hardware profiles (specs + OS images) by 2026-04-23 for on-prem validation. (customer action)
- AI-5: Diego Martinez - send updated pilot runbook and gating checklist to ACME and internal CS by 2026-04-22. (planned)
- AI-6: Liam O'Connor & runtime team - investigate cold-start spike root cause and propose mitigation (KV cache pre-warm / warm pool) by 2026-04-28. (medium)
- AI-7: Maya Chen - prepare pilot cutover checklist + communication template for ACME by 2026-05-04. (owned)
- AI-8: Sarah Patel - draft incident response runbook tailored for ACME pilot and share with ACME infosec by 2026-04-29. (blocking)
- AI-9: Ethan Li (ACME) - schedule two network alignment calls next week (Tue/Thu AM) and share calendar invites by 2026-04-21. (customer)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: If HSM provisioning is delayed, can we run the pilot using Redwood-managed KMS with data access controls? (need legal + ACME approval)
- Q2: What is acceptable cold-start tail for ACME? confirm with ACME PM (Ethan) whether warm pool increases cost acceptable.
- Q3: Confirm storage cost delta for 90-day audit logs (finance required).

Next meeting:
- Weekly sync: 2026-04-27 09:00 PT (same invite)
- Suggested focus: peering confirmation, installer release status, KMS provisioning update, mitigation plan for cold-start spikes.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Push to get hardware profiles early — on-prem validation always stalls when we get vague specs.
- Consider a lightweight demo for ACME infra team showing warm pool vs no-warm pool impact (visuals + numbers) - might help procurement sign-off.
- Keep a tight list of rollback criteria for pilot cutover; want automatic fallback to hosted API if on-prem path fails.

Attachments to add: pilot-runbook-v1.md, installer-changelog-v0.9.1.md, kms-hsm-integration-note.md

End notes: capture updates into Confluence page after items are closed; Diego to maintain customer-facing runbook.

-- Maya
